docs.title: Workspace
docs.text: A workspace provides shared object storage, virtual Kubernetes clusters, an OCI registry, and a Data service. Teams can share buckets or publish files for anyone to download. Browser sessions provide an editor and terminal when needed; the other services run independently.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
Follow the quickstart to create a workspace, access its virtual cluster, delegate namespace access, and push a registry package. The STAC notebooks publish satellite data and serve search APIs.

Use the notebook guide to choose an example and check what it needs before you run it.

For an existing workspace, use Concepts to add a colleague, share a bucket with another team, publish a dataset, or start a session.

docs.title: Set up the service
docs.text:
Operators can use installation to set up the shared services. Use IAM integration to give people and jobs the access they need, and operational controls to set session resources and network access.

The architecture page shows how the API, Crossplane packages, and runtime services fit together.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
Workspaces provide shared storage, virtual clusters, a registry, and Data. Members can share buckets with another workspace or publish files for readers without an account.

Open your workspace dashboard and select Management to manage members, buckets, sessions, and services. The available tabs and actions depend on your workspace role.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
A Storage resource defines buckets, a storage identity, access requests, grants, and lifecycle rules. Workspace members use that identity and its bucket permissions. A bucket grant lets another workspace use selected data with its own credentials, so teams can share a dataset without copying it.

A discoverable bucket can appear in another workspace’s access-request list. Its owner still has to approve access. The receiving workspace then uses its own storage credentials to reach the bucket.

Permission Access ReadOnly List and read objects. ReadWrite List, read, write, and delete objects. WriteOnly List, write, and delete objects, without reading their contents. None Record that access is not granted.

For manifest-based setup, backends that resolve requests from peer Storage resources also need storages.pkg.internal/discoverable: "true" on the owner resource. The per-bucket discoverable field advertises the bucket; it is not a storage policy.

Lifecycle rules belong to spec.buckets[].lifecycleRules. A rule selects the whole bucket with * or a prefix such as tmp/*. Notify reports matching objects; Delete removes them. Set exactly one age (minAge, such as 12h) or UTC cutoff (at).

See the provider’s permission model for backend details.

docs.title: Create a bucket
docs.text:
Open Buckets, add a unique bucket name, and save it. Start the name with your workspace name, for example ws-test-20261024071434-test. Wait for storage to finish creating the bucket before uploading files.

Mark a bucket as discoverable to let other workspaces find it and request access. This does not make its objects public. See public shares for public downloads.

docs.title: Share a bucket with another workspace
docs.text:
1. In the receiving workspace, request access to the owner’s discoverable bucket.
  2. In the owner’s workspace, open Requested Buckets, review the permission, and select Grant bucket access.
  3. Wait for the storage policy to update.
  4. In the receiving workspace, use its existing storage credentials to access the shared bucket.

Use ReadOnly for a reader. The permission table describes each level.

docs.title: Virtual clusters and registry
docs.text:
On the demo, a new workspace includes the vc0 virtual Kubernetes cluster and a managed OCI registry. Their ready connection settings appear on the dashboard. Workspace administrators receive virtual cluster administration automatically. They can add namespace profiles in Management > Vclusters and exchange a user token to delegate one profile.

The registry stores container images and OCI packages in the workspace bucket. Its connection supplies a separate registry user and password. Use ORAS to push a file package, or a container client to push an image. The Workspace Management notebook shows the API calls, delegated access, registry login, and package push and pull. See virtual cluster access for standalone kubectl commands.

docs.title: Datalabs and sessions
docs.text:
A Datalab resource defines the team’s users, sessions, and shared services. Start a session when you need an editor, a terminal, or a place to run code. Each named session has a persistent home volume, so you can stop it and keep your files for the next run.

Sessions share the workspace’s storage identity and managed services. A session can use a host-cluster namespace or its own virtual Kubernetes control plane. See operational controls for the settings.

docs.title: Start or stop a session
docs.text:
Open Sessions to add a named session or change its state. Opening its Datalab link starts a stopped session when the API supports on-demand access.

Shared storage, Data, and managed databases have separate lifecycles. See session controls for the initial mode and storage limits.

docs.title: Managed services
docs.text: Use a managed service when your code needs a database, cache, or vector store shared within the workspace. PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Qdrant need their operators installed in the platform.

docs.title: Add a managed service
docs.text:
Use Stores to request an available service. The platform operator must install and configure its database operator first.

An operator can also add a service to the existing Datalab configuration. For example, this block requests a MongoDB store named test:

spec:
  documentStores:
    test:
      storage: 1Gi

Keep the Datalab’s other fields when adding this block. The session receives MONGO_TEST_URI after the service is ready. Stop and start the session to load changed connection settings.

Provider Datalab’s usage guide describes the PostgreSQL, cache, vector, and registry fields. Its application examples cover tools such as MLflow.

docs.title: Data access and sharing
docs.text:
PackageR is the workspace storage browser. The Data service is enabled by default. An operator can give it a permanent address such as https://<workspace-name>.lab.example.org. The Datalab’s Data tab opens that same service.

With a permanent address, storage browsing and public shares work without a running compute session. Sign in to browse private workspace data. A public share or presigned download link can be used without a workspace account.

docs.title: Public shares
docs.text:
Put files in the public/ folder of the bucket named after the workspace. For ws-bob, this is s3://ws-bob/public/. The default share exposes that folder for public browsing and downloads. A public/ folder in another bucket is not shared automatically.

Open /share/public/ on the Data hostname. Every file placed in this folder is public. Upload files through PackageR when writes are allowed, or use the backing storage endpoint and its credentials.

docs.title: Presigned download links
docs.text:
A presigned URL gives temporary access to one object. In PackageR, select a file, open Info, then select Show beside Presigned URL.

This URL points to object storage. It works until it expires, and the recipient needs network access to that storage endpoint.

A public-share download route can redirect to a fresh presigned URL. Share that route when you need a link that lasts longer than one signed URL. Workspace Management checks both download paths against the uploaded bytes.

docs.title: STAC catalogues
docs.text:
Use STAC to describe when data was collected, which area it covers, and where to download its files. Applications can read these descriptions to choose the data they need.

Put a STAC GeoParquet file at public/catalog.parquet to publish a catalogue through the existing Data service. PackageR reads it when someone requests the catalogue and builds Collection and Item responses with public asset links. Relative asset paths resolve within the share folder.

Start with the Vienna notebook to publish satellite images and let other people download them. It crops three images, adds descriptions for the cropped area, and checks public and authenticated S3 downloads.

The registration notebook uploads with Portolan under published/ and demonstrates API search in the workspace vCluster. It copies the assets under public/ with stacpkg and keeps the source files. PackageR serves the public catalogue through the Data service, with HTTP asset links. A third flow deploys CNCF Distribution in that vCluster, pushes a metadata package, and starts a second API from its digest. The notebook guide compares these views and their setup.

docs.title: S3 clients
docs.text:
The optional Data S3 endpoint lets AWS tools read data through the Data hostname. It uses path-style requests, and is read only. Uploads use the backing object-storage endpoint.

Signing setting Value Endpoint The workspace’s permanent Data URL. Access key ID The workspace name. Secret access key The same workspace name. Session token A valid Keycloak access token.

The signing names are public identifiers. The token must include the workspace name in aud and ws_access, ws_admin, or ws_api under that workspace’s client roles. Human users can use device login through the central client. A service can use the generated workspace client’s credentials.

The endpoint supports bucket and object listing, HEAD, GET, and byte-range GET. It rejects uploads and S3 query-presigned requests. S3 reads of public/ objects still need a token; public-share links use a separate route.

Operators enable S3 through the environment configuration. The Vienna notebook refreshes its device login before the S3 and AWS CLI steps and checks the downloaded files by SHA-256.

docs.title: Automatic token renewal
docs.text:
For service access, use scripts/s3-credentials.py as an AWS credential_process. The script returns the signing values, an OAuth access token, and its expiry time. AWS CLI and Boto3 can run it again when they need fresh credentials. See the AWS process credential documentation.

Run these commands from the repository root. Install Python and AWS CLI first. Replace the workspace name, Data URL, and Keycloak realm URL with your service settings. The workspace OAuth client must have the audience and role described above.

aws configure set region us-east-1 --profile ws-alice
aws configure set endpoint_url https://ws-alice.lab.example.org --profile ws-alice
aws configure set s3.addressing_style path --profile ws-alice
aws configure set credential_process \
  "python3 \"$PWD/scripts/s3-credentials.py\" --tenant ws-alice --issuer https://keycloak.example.org/realms/eoepca" \
  --profile ws-alice

These commands add a profile to ~/.aws/config. The process command uses the script’s absolute path. It belongs in the config file; do not copy the returned token into ~/.aws/credentials. The resulting profile has this form:

[profile ws-alice]
region = us-east-1
endpoint_url = https://ws-alice.lab.example.org
credential_process = python3 "/absolute/path/to/workspace/scripts/s3-credentials.py" --tenant ws-alice --issuer https://keycloak.example.org/realms/eoepca
s3 =
    addressing_style = path

Enter the OAuth client secret once for the current terminal. The hidden prompt keeps it out of shell history. The helper reads CLIENT_SECRET when AWS starts it.

CLIENT_SECRET="$(python3 -c 'import getpass; print(getpass.getpass("OAuth client secret: "))')"
export CLIENT_SECRET
unset AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
aws s3 ls s3://ws-alice/ --profile ws-alice

Boto3 can use the same profile from a process started in that terminal:

import boto3

session = boto3.Session(profile_name="ws-alice")
s3 = session.client("s3")
objects = s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket="ws-alice", MaxKeys=10)

Keep CLIENT_SECRET available while these clients run so the helper can get new tokens. Run unset CLIENT_SECRET when you finish. This profile provides read-only access through the Data endpoint. Use the registration notebook for uploads to backing storage.

docs.title: Membership
docs.text:
Add members so colleagues can use the workspace’s data and services. A workspace role controls dashboard and management actions. Members who can view storage credentials use the workspace’s full storage policy, including its existing bucket grants.

The owner of another workspace approves any additional bucket grant. See IAM roles for the management permissions.

docs.title: Add a member
docs.text:
1. Open Members.
  2. Add an existing Keycloak username and select its workspace role.
  3. Save the change.
  4. Ask the new member to sign in again to load the assigned roles.

Give workspace administrator access to people who need to manage members, buckets, sessions, or stores.

docs.title: Check a workspace that is still starting
docs.text:
An operator can inspect status without reading credential values:

kubectl get storage,datalab -n workspace
workspace_name=ws-test-20261024071434
kubectl describe datalab "$workspace_name" -n workspace

Set workspace_name to the name printed by your notebook. Check the reported conditions and events. If storage works but the Data hostname does not, check its workload, HTTPRoute, Gateway listener, certificate reference, DNS, and public load-balancer route.

docs.title: Workspace Management¶
docs.text:
Create a workspace, use its virtual Kubernetes cluster and container registry, and share a sample file.

Oscar creates the workspace for Alice. Alice downloads its connection settings, adds a namespace access profile, delegates that profile to a process, and pushes a small OCI package to the registry.

docs.title: Run the notebook¶
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv sync
uv run jupyter lab docs/workspace-management.ipynb

Install kubectl and the ORAS CLI. ORAS can push files as OCI packages to a Docker-compatible registry without a Docker daemon.

The notebook uses the public service settings in eoepca-demo.env and the sample docs/catalog.v1.parquet. Tokens and credentials stay in kernel memory or private temporary files. They are not displayed.

docs.title: 1. Load the service settings¶
docs.text:
The central public client workspace-api needs S256 PKCE and Device Authorization Grant enabled. Set WORKSPACE_CLIENT_ID to that client in the settings file.

Load the settings and check the service addresses:

docs.title: 2. Sign in as the owner and creator¶
docs.text:
Enter alice, bob, or eric as the owner and complete device login as that user.

If the owner cannot create workspaces, sign in as oscar when prompted. Use a fresh private browser window for each account. See roles for the required access.

docs.title: 3. Create a workspace¶
docs.text:
The API adds ws- to the requested name, so this example creates ws-test-<UTC timestamp>.

On this demo, workspace creation also requests a vc0 virtual Kubernetes cluster. Provider Datalab enables a managed Docker-compatible OCI registry and the Data service by default. The registry stores packages in the workspace bucket. Platform settings can change these defaults; the connection list below shows what is ready.

The owner receives workspace administration and the virtual cluster's administrator role automatically.

docs.title: 4. Open the workspace¶
docs.text: Sign in again as the owner to obtain the new workspace roles. The dashboard provides connection downloads. Management has the member, bucket, service, and vcluster settings.

docs.title: 5. Access the default virtual cluster¶
docs.text:
GET /workspaces/<workspace>?resolve_connections=* returns ready service connections, including the public kubeconfig. The dashboard uses the same endpoint.

Select the built-in administrator profile and save its kubeconfig. Supply the owner's access token separately through DATALAB_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE. This uses the human login from step 4. See device login with kubectl to start a separate kubectl login.

These calls use the short-lived notebook token. The offline CLI cache applies when kubectl starts its own device login. See login lifetimes.

The default kubeconfig grants no permissions by itself. Provider Datalab has already assigned the owner the vcluster_vc0_cluster-admin role.

docs.title: 6. Add a namespace access profile¶
docs.text:
Open Management > Vclusters > Add access profile. Enter name demo, namespace demo, and role edit. The form below is from the demo UI. The next cell sends the same request as its Add access profile button.

POST /workspaces/<workspace>/vclusters/vc0/groups
Content-Type: application/json

{"name":"demo","namespace":"demo","role":"edit"}

This creates a profile and namespace permissions. It does not issue a token. Wait for the provider to publish the profile as ready before downloading it.

docs.title: 7. Delegate the profile to a process¶
docs.text:
Sign in again to obtain the new vcluster_vc0_demo role. Exchange that user token by calling:

GET /workspaces/<workspace>/token?scope=<workspace>:vclusters_vc0_demo
Authorization: Bearer <owner-access-token>

Workspace API performs the exchange with its stored client credentials. The result keeps the owner's identity and contains ws_api and the selected profile role. It contains no refresh token or administrator role. Without the scope query, this endpoint returns a service-account token, which has no vcluster access.

Give the process the exchanged token and the selected kubeconfig. It needs no client secret and has no browser prompt.

The recipient must obtain another exchanged token after expires_in. The owner's offline CLI login does not extend it.

The namespace limit applies to Kubernetes. The ws_api role also permits reading workspace service credentials through Workspace API.

docs.title: 8. Push a package to the registry¶
docs.text:
The registry:primary connection contains the registry endpoint and its user and password. These are registry credentials, separate from the OAuth token. Download them through the workspace connection API or the dashboard's registry card.

Use oras login --password-stdin to avoid putting the password in command arguments. The example uses a private registry configuration file so it does not read or change your normal Docker login.

Push hello.txt as an OCI package, pull it again, and compare the bytes. The managed registry stores it in the workspace bucket. No registry Deployment or volume is needed inside vc0.

docs.title: 9. Upload one sample via S3¶
docs.text: Upload catalog.v1.parquet via backing S3, then copy one preview from its first Item into workspace storage.

docs.title: 10. Check a temporary download¶
docs.text:
Generate one presigned URL with the S3 client. Download the sample from backing object storage, compare its checksum, and display it. The URL expires after 15 minutes and stays out of saved output.

This cell signs the URL locally with boto3. Step 11 shows the PackageR HTTP API that returns a presigned URL in JSON.

docs.title: 11. Check a public download via the PackageR HTTP API¶
docs.text:
Copy the sample via backing S3 into public/. Anyone with its public-share link can read it.

To get a presigned URL in a JSON response, call:

GET <Data URL>/api/public/share/public/<filename>?presign=true

Read the presignedURL field. To get an HTTP redirect to that URL instead, add &followRedirect=true. The client follows the redirect and downloads the bytes from object storage. The permanent PackageR link can issue a new signed URL when the old one expires.

docs.title: Result¶
docs.text:
The workspace has storage, a virtual cluster, a namespace profile for delegated access, and a managed OCI registry. The owner can also share files through expiring S3 links and permanent public-share routes.

The workspace, uploaded files, and registry package stay available. Use the printed workspace name for Vienna. The STAC API notebooks need the additional services listed in the notebook guide.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
A workspace brings together a team’s storage, access roles, sessions, and shared services. Users request these through the Workspace API. They can keep published data available while compute sessions are stopped.

The API records the requested configuration as Storage and Datalab resources in Kubernetes. Crossplane runs their compositions to create and update storage, identity resources, sessions, and services. The diagram shows which component handles each part of a workspace request.

flowchart TD
    UI[Workspace dashboard and management] --> API[Workspace API]
    API --> S[Storage resource]
    API --> D[Datalab resource]
    S --> PS[Provider Storage]
    PS --> B[S3 buckets and storage identities]
    D --> PD[Provider Datalab]
    PD --> IAM[Keycloak clients, groups, and roles]
    PD --> DATA[Shared Data service]
    PD --> VC[Workspace virtual Kubernetes clusters]
    PD --> REG[OCI registry backed by workspace storage]
    PD --> SESSION[Named Datalab sessions]
    PD --> STORES[Optional managed stores]

docs.title: Storage and runtime
docs.text:
Provider Storage creates buckets, storage identities, policies, and credential Secrets. Backend compositions support MinIO, AWS S3, OTC OBS, OVHcloud, and CloudFerro.

Provider Datalab uses those storage credentials. It creates Data, the managed OCI registry, requested stores, workspace vClusters, and declared browser sessions. The registry stores its packages in the workspace bucket. The STAC notebooks use clusters configured under spec.vclusters; Workspace API supplies their kubeconfig profiles. These services run independently of browser sessions.

The API and UI run as separate components from the composition packages. The pipeline chart installs the Storage and Datalab packages and their shared configuration. It does not deploy the Workspace API or UI.

docs.title: Shared configuration
docs.text:
Use an EnvironmentConfig to apply common platform settings to workspaces. It holds the domain, IAM, storage, network, and default resource settings used by the compositions. A resource selects it with its environment annotation or label.

The pipeline chart creates one EnvironmentConfig, named datalab by default. Educates has separate installation values for the session ingress domain, class, and TLS Secret. Those values must match the Datalab environment settings. See installation.

Crossplane updates resources from the declared configuration. An operator can use GitOps or the Workspace API to manage that configuration. Assign each field to one writer so the API and GitOps do not replace each other’s changes.

docs.title: Request paths
docs.text:
The platform gateway protects the Workspace API and browser session routes. The permanent Data endpoint has its own OAuth protection. Public shares and authenticated Data S3 reads use separate routes on the Data hostname.

Workloads created inside a vCluster still run on the host cluster. The host controls their network access, admission rules, and public routes. IAM integration describes token checks; operational controls describes the Workspace settings.

docs.title: IAM integration
docs.text: People need to sign in to manage a workspace. Jobs need access that works without a person at a browser. Keycloak provides both user tokens and service-account tokens; workspace roles determine which API actions each caller can use. Storage policies control S3 object access.

docs.title: Login and workspace clients
docs.text:
Use a central public client, such as workspace-api, for user login to the API, UI, and shared session routes. For the notebooks, enable Device Authorization Grant and S256 PKCE on this client. A user signs in once and receives the roles for their workspaces.

Provider Datalab creates a separate confidential client for each workspace. Its ID matches the Datalab name. It enables service accounts, browser login, device login, and restricted user-token exchange. It limits role scope and disables implicit and password grants.

Resource Example Use Central public client workspace-api Browser and device login for people. Workspace confidential client ws-alice Workspace roles and machine tokens. User group ws-alice Assign ws_access. Admin group ws-alice-admin Assign ws_admin. OAuth client Secret Resolved from status.oauth2 Supply the workspace client ID and secret to authorized callers.

The client secret authenticates the workspace OAuth client. It supports service-account token requests and human device login. The STAC notebooks use Alice’s login to obtain their workspace credentials.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Workspace API access ws_access View workspace connections, OAuth client credentials, members, buckets, stores, sessions, and vclusters. ws_admin All user actions; manage members, buckets, stores, sessions, and vclusters; issue workspace tokens. ws_api Read storage and service connection credentials; no OAuth client credentials. admin on workspace-api Platform administration across workspaces, including workspace creation.

The token-issuance permission is ISSUE_TOKENS; ws_admin includes it. The workspace service account has ws_api by default. This role cannot manage a workspace or open interactive browser routes.

A workspace role limits management actions. Members with access to the shared storage credentials use the same storage policy. Bucket grants control which other workspace buckets that identity can use.

docs.title: Token claims
docs.text:
The gateway checks the token signature, issuer, expiry, audience, and route policy. The Workspace API reads the validated bearer token:

  • aud includes the API audience, normally workspace-api.
  • preferred_username identifies the caller.
  • resource_access.<workspace>.roles holds the workspace roles.
  • resource_access.workspace-api.roles can hold the platform admin role.

This example gives Alice user access to one workspace and administrator access to another:

{
  "aud": ["workspace-api"],
  "azp": "workspace-api",
  "preferred_username": "alice",
  "resource_access": {
    "ws-alice": {"roles": ["ws_access"]},
    "ws-bob": {"roles": ["ws_admin"]}
  }
}

For generated workspace clients, add the API audience through EnvironmentConfig.data.iam.extraAudiences. Configure the central user client to emit the required audiences and workspace roles as well. Refresh a user token after a new workspace or membership is created.

The Data S3 endpoint also requires the workspace name in aud. See S3 clients for its signing values.

docs.title: Machine access
docs.text:
A client-credentials token identifies the workspace service account. It has ws_api under the workspace client roles and a username such as service-account-ws-alice.

Use OAuth client credentials for a scheduled upload or a task delegated to another service. The job requests a token with its client ID and secret, calls the Workspace API for storage credentials, and passes those credentials to its upload tool. No workspace team member needs to be present or sign in through a browser. The token needs the API audience and the target workspace’s ws_api role.

The STAC registration notebook uses Alice’s login to obtain storage credentials for Portolan uploads and stacpkg relocation. For a scheduled upload, use the machine-access flow above and get the client secret from the job’s secret store. The first API’s startup Secret supplies storage access until it switches to public HTTP metadata. The notebook’s OCI publisher uses an internal Distribution Service in the workspace vCluster.

The API also has /workspaces/<workspace-name>/token for callers with ISSUE_TOKENS or platform administration. Without scope, it returns a workspace service-account token with ws_api. With configured profile scopes, it exchanges the caller’s user token for selected profile roles. See delegated access.

docs.title: Virtual cluster access
docs.text:
The dashboard supplies connection settings separately from caller credentials. Provider Datalab automatically grants workspace administrators ws_admin and each configured instance’s built-in vcluster administrator role. Alice therefore already has vcluster_vc0_cluster-admin. She uses the administrator profile for device login with her human identity; no separate role assignment is needed. Current profiles request offline access and cache the CLI login for up to 30 days, subject to Keycloak offline-session limits. Notebook logins through the central public client have a separate lifetime.

For a process, Alice requests an exchanged token for one additional profile. The recipient supplies that token through DATALAB_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE and uses the downloaded profile without a browser prompt. The token keeps Alice’s subject and selected roles. A namespace kubeconfig alone cannot restrict a token that still has administrator roles.

Follow Access a workspace virtual cluster for UI downloads, token exchange, namespace checks, and login lifetimes. The Provider Datalab guide describes the underlying profiles, cache, and revocation limits.

docs.title: Route protection
docs.text:
Protect the shared UI and session routes with the workspace roles in resource_access. A service owned by one workspace can use its confidential client and require the expected audience, client ID, and roles.

Provider Datalab supplies OAuth protection for the permanent Data browser. Public-share routes allow anonymous downloads. The read-only Data S3 endpoint validates its own signed requests and bearer tokens. Configure the Data issuer URLs in the installation values.

docs.title: Operational controls
docs.text: Use these settings to choose when sessions start, how much storage and memory they can request, and which services they can reach. The platform operator manages the host cluster, public routing, and storage services.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
Choose whether a new workspace starts a session immediately, starts one when a user opens it, or has no default session. The Workspace API’s SESSION_MODE sets this initial state:

Value Initial state auto Declare default as stopped; opening its Datalab link starts it. on Declare default as started. off Do not declare a default session.

Automatic shutdown needs an operator job or policy. The API does not stop idle sessions by itself.

A stopped session keeps its home PVC. Object storage and shared Data or database services have separate lifecycles. Set spec.quota for session memory, volume size, and budget. spec.overallQuota.storage limits requested PVC storage in the Datalab environment namespace; it does not cover object storage or PVCs in other namespaces.

docs.title: Kubernetes access
docs.text:
Workspace clusters are declared under spec.vclusters. They run independently of browser sessions. Administrators can add namespace profiles and download kubeconfigs through Workspace API.

Browser sessions can use the host control plane with a session namespace role, or their own virtual control plane. Workloads still use host-cluster nodes and remain subject to host policies.

Use spec.security to select the Pod security level, Kubernetes token access, namespace role, and external egress. Omitted fields use EnvironmentConfig.data.defaults.security, then provider defaults. Configure the host’s admission policies and resource limits separately.

docs.title: Network access
docs.text:
Allow the connections that session code needs, such as HTTPS to a data provider or access to platform storage. The network plugin must enforce Kubernetes NetworkPolicy. Policies add their allowed connections together.

Generated policy Created when Allows deny-egress By default No outbound traffic on its own. allow-namespace-egress By default Pods in the same runtime namespace. allow-vcluster-egress vCluster is enabled The session’s virtual API. allow-dns-egress External egress, vCluster, or Data is enabled Cluster DNS. allow-external-egress External egress is enabled and external CIDRs are set The configured external CIDRs, with exclusions. allow-internal-egress Valid network.internalEgress entries exist Selected Pods and ports in other namespaces.

The per-Datalab spec.security.externalEgress setting overrides the environment default. An empty external CIDR list creates no broad external allow rule.

Set the cluster Service and Pod CIDRs and any blocked ranges in the EnvironmentConfig. The provider excludes them from broad external rules. Use network.internalEgress for selected storage, identity, and other platform services.

network.excludePolicies can omit generated policies by name. Data services also have their own policies. Check the policies actually installed in each namespace when testing a connection.

docs.title: Data and public routes
docs.text:
Use a permanent Data address for downloads that must stay available when a compute session stops. spec.data.enabled defaults to true and cannot change after Datalab creation. Set it when creating the resource. spec.data.readOnlyMount controls Data browser permissions; storage IAM still controls object access. The optional Data S3 endpoint is always read only.

Manage public routes in the host cluster. For a permanent Data address, the public load balancer must reach the selected Gateway listener, and that listener must terminate TLS. Storage can be ready before the Data workload and its route are ready.

See environment configuration for routing values and IAM integration for authentication.

docs.title: Persistent data
docs.text: Session files use PVCs; datasets use object storage; managed stores have their own volumes. Stopping a session keeps its home volume. See Operations for backups, retention, host security, and platform recovery.

docs.title: Configure Workspace
docs.text: Follow the component guides for installation. The EOEPCA+ deployment links below use a fixed revision with the configuration examples.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Component and installation guide Purpose Documented version requirement Kubernetes Runs controllers and workloads. Needs NetworkPolicy enforcement and persistent volumes. No Workspace minimum stated. Educates 3.8 bundles clients for 1.33–1.36. Ingress controller (APISIX) Routes sessions; needs WebSockets, wildcard DNS, and TLS. No minimum stated; see the runtime requirements. Gateway API controller (Envoy Gateway) Routes Data when using HTTPRoute; see the deployment. HTTPRoute with cross-namespace routes; header regular expressions for S3. External PostgreSQL needs TLSRoute v1. Crossplane Reconciles Storage and Datalab resources. >= 2.0, < 3.0. Keycloak Manages workspace identities, groups, roles, and OAuth clients. 26.2 or later for standard token exchange; no provisioning minimum stated. Educates Provides browser sessions, terminals, and editors. The notebooks use workspace vClusters instead. Pinned to 3.8.0; no minimum stated. Kyverno Enforces the selected Educates security policies. Bundled policies require 1.11.0 or later. Extra platform policies can require newer versions. S3-compatible object storage Stores workspace data. Backend supported by Provider Storage; no common minimum stated. Provider Storage Creates buckets, storage identities, grants, and credential Secrets. >= 0.4.0 for the current Workspace API. Provider Datalab Creates membership, Data services, workspace vClusters, browser sessions, and managed services. Documented API requirement: >= 0.12.0. Install provider and function dependencies, namespaced ProviderConfigs, and RBAC through the provider guides. Pins and tested versions do not establish minimum versions.

Without rm-workspace-api, create Storage and Datalab resources through Kubernetes or GitOps. You then have no Workspace management UI, Workspace HTTP API, or Workspace token-exchange endpoint. The notebook quickstart needs the API.

docs.title: 1. Set the environment
docs.text:
Adapt the deployment’s pipeline values: IAM URLs and realm, storage endpoint, ingress domain and certificate, Gateway listeners, and Pod and Service network ranges. For browser sessions, keep the Educates ingress values consistent. The provider guide lists fields and defaults.

The workspace-pipeline chart installs the configuration packages and creates the EnvironmentConfig. It copies environmentconfig into EnvironmentConfig.data, except for name and annotations. The example’s prerelease package overrides differ from the chart defaults. Keep exact pins in your deployment.

The example uses the EnvironmentConfig name datalab. Select it on each resource with an annotation or label:

Resource Key Value Storage storages.pkg.internal/environment datalab Datalab datalabs.pkg.internal/environment datalab

For resources created by Workspace API, set PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT=datalab.

docs.title: 2. Create a workspace
docs.text:
With Workspace API, configure its deployment and accounts and roles, then run Workspace Management. It creates a workspace and waits for storage, Data, the virtual cluster, and the managed registry.

For direct Kubernetes use, save the provider’s Storage example as storage.yaml and Datalab example as datalab.yaml. Adapt them before applying:

  1. Use ws-example for both resource names and the Storage principal, in namespace workspace. Choose a unique bucket name. Remove sample bucket access requests and grants.
  2. Set both environment selectors from the table above. Select the storage backend with spec.crossplane.compositionSelector.matchLabels.provider, for example minio.
  3. Set the EnvironmentConfig’s storage.secretNamespace to workspace. Storage creates a Secret named after its principal; Datalab reads it using its resource name.
  4. Set an existing Keycloak username in spec.users. For the STAC notebooks, use the spec.vclusters configuration from the workspace example. Omit spec.sessions unless you need browser sessions.
kubectl apply -n workspace -f storage.yaml
kubectl wait -n workspace --for=condition=Ready storage/ws-example --timeout=300s
kubectl apply -n workspace -f datalab.yaml
kubectl wait -n workspace --for=condition=Ready datalab/ws-example --timeout=300s
kubectl get storages,datalabs -n workspace

docs.title: 3. Use the workspace
docs.text: With Workspace API, continue with the quickstart. The notebook guide lists services needed for each example. For direct Kubernetes use, check Datalab status for service and session addresses.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Create a workspace, use its virtual cluster and registry, and publish data.

Start with Workspace Management if you need a test workspace. Then choose Vienna for public and S3 downloads, or STAC registration for an automated upload and search APIs. Use STAC with managed PostgreSQL to register the supplied three-Item sample in a PgSTAC database. The notebook guide lists the services each example needs.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
These examples use eoepca-demo. The repository includes public service settings in eoepca-demo.env and a three-Item sample in docs/catalog.v1.parquet.

Requirement Used for alice and oscar accounts Alice owns the workspace; Oscar has the workspace-api platform admin role and creates it. Storage and a permanent Data address Upload files, browse public shares, and download data. Data S3 endpoint enabled Run the authenticated S3 and AWS CLI steps. Workspace vCluster with an API kubeconfig profile Run the STAC API notebooks. Registration deploys its registry in this vCluster.

For a new platform, start with components and environment configuration. An operator sets up the accounts and roles. For another deployment, change the service settings and account names.

docs.title: 1. Create a workspace
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv sync
uv run jupyter lab docs/workspace-management.ipynb

Run Workspace Management. Sign in as Alice with device login, then as Oscar when the notebook asks for an administrator.

The notebook creates ws-test-<UTC timestamp>. On this demo, the workspace includes storage, a vc0 virtual cluster, a managed OCI registry, and Data. Alice signs in again to obtain her new workspace roles. The notebook shows the same HTTP call as the UI to add a namespace profile, exchanges a token for that profile, and pushes and pulls a small package with ORAS. Use the printed workspace name to run Vienna in this workspace. The STAC API notebooks use the preconfigured ws-alice services.

The API returns a name, for example:

{"name": "ws-test-20261024071434"}

The dashboard address is WORKSPACE_API_ENDPOINT/<workspace-name>. The API adds the configured ws- prefix to the preferred name.

docs.title: 2. Open the workspace
docs.text:
Open the dashboard link as Alice. Check the storage connection and Data link. Run the notebooks from your repository checkout. The STAC API notebooks download their workspace vCluster profiles through Workspace API.

For kubectl access, follow Access a workspace virtual cluster. It shows device login as Alice, the offline CLI cache, and token exchange for a process limited to the demo profile. The exchanged token has its own short lifetime and no refresh token.

Workspace Management uploads the sample catalogue and one available preview image. It checks the image through an expiring S3 link and a permanent public-share link. Both downloads must match the uploaded bytes.

docs.title: 3. Publish and read satellite images
docs.text:
Open Vienna imagery with STAC and S3. Use Alice’s existing ws-alice, or enter the workspace name from step 1.

Use this example to publish images that other people can inspect and download. The catalogue describes each cropped image, so a reader can find its date, area, and files. The notebook:

  1. Crops three Sentinel-2 images over Vienna and creates previews.
  2. Uploads those files and a STAC GeoParquet catalogue.
  3. Reads the published STAC items and public image links.
  4. Uses device login for authenticated S3 reads and the AWS CLI.
  5. Checks a byte-range read and compares download checksums.

Existing image files with matching checksums are kept. A different image at the same key stops the upload. The shared catalogue retains other datasets.

Open /share/public/ on the Data hostname to browse the published files:

docs.title: 4. Publish, relocate, and serve STAC data
docs.text:
Run Register STAC metadata from your checkout. Sign in as Alice. The notebook gets storage credentials and the ws-alice/vc0/demo kubeconfig through Workspace API. The example resources configure that profile and its namespace.

Flow 1 prepares three Sentinel-5P cloud fraction observations from the DLR GeoService STAC endpoint for use around Vienna. Portolan describes the clips and uploads them under published/. A first workspace vCluster API demonstrates search through a local Kubernetes Service proxy. Flow 2 copies the assets to public/ with stacpkg and keeps the source files. The metadata then uses PackageR HTTP asset links.

PackageR serves the public catalogue through the Data service. Preview it in MoreGeo STAC Browser and update the first API with the public metadata. Flow 3 deploys CNCF Distribution inside the workspace vCluster. A publisher Job pushes the metadata package, and a second API pulls it by digest. The notebook guide compares the views.

Each registration run selects three observations. It keeps older published data and shared catalogue entries. The notebooks leave the workspace, uploaded files, and OCI package available for inspection. Registry artifacts stay on its PVC across Pod restarts.

docs.title: 5. Work with a team
docs.text:
Use the management page to add members and manage bucket access. Members use the workspace’s storage identity. To use a bucket owned by another workspace, request access and have its owner approve the grant.

See Concepts for the access model and steps for managing members, bucket grants, and sessions.

docs.title: 6. Use managed services
docs.text:
A workspace can request PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, or Qdrant when the platform has the required operators. Use the Stores tab when these services are available. Their connection settings appear on the dashboard and in new Datalab sessions.

For operator configuration and application examples, see Add a managed service.

PARQUET_TYPE = "application/vnd.apache.parquet"

    "https://stac-extensions.github.io/alternate-assets/v1.2.0/schema.json"
)
PROCESSING_SCHEMA = "https://stac-extensions.github.io/processing/v1.2.0/schema.json"


class EmptyClipError(ValueError):
    """The observation has no valid pixels in the requested area."""


def recent_clips(candidates, catalog_dir, collection_id, bbox, count=3):
    """Clip the latest usable observation per day from newest-first candidates."""
    products = []
    days = set()
    for item in candidates:
        if item.datetime is None or "cf" not in item.assets:
            continue
        day = item.datetime.date()
        if day in days:
            continue
        try:
            product = clip_items([item], catalog_dir, collection_id, bbox)[0]
        except EmptyClipError:
            continue
        products.append(product)
        days.add(day)
        if len(products) == count:
            return sorted(products, key=lambda product: product["source"].datetime)
    raise ValueError(f"Found {len(products)} usable observations; need {count}.")


def public_url(data_url: str, key: str) -> str:
    """Return a permanent download route for a key below public/."""
    path = PurePosixPath(key)
    if path.is_absolute() or ".." in path.parts or path.parts[:1] != ("public",):
        raise ValueError("The object key must be below public/.")
    relative = str(path.relative_to("public"))
    if relative == ".":
        raise ValueError("Set a file path below public/.")
    return (
        f"{require_https(data_url)}/api/public/share/public/"
        f"{quote(relative, safe='/')}?presign=true&followRedirect=true"
    )


def clip_items(source_items, catalog_dir: Path, collection_id: str, bbox):
    """Write COGs and previews on the source grid, with no resampling."""
    if len(bbox) != 4 or not (
        -180 <= bbox[0] < bbox[2] <= 180 and -90 <= bbox[1] < bbox[3] <= 90
    ):
        raise ValueError("Set a valid longitude and latitude bounding box.")
    products = []
    for item in source_items:
        item_id = f"{collection_id}-{item.datetime:%Y%m%d}"
        directory = catalog_dir / collection_id / item_id
        cog = directory / "cf.tif"
        raw = directory / "source-clip.tif"
        with rasterio.Env(
            GDAL_DISABLE_READDIR_ON_OPEN="EMPTY_DIR",
            GDAL_HTTP_TIMEOUT="60",
            GDAL_HTTP_MAX_RETRY="2",
        ):
            with rasterio.open(item.assets["cf"].href) as source:
                if source.crs != rasterio.CRS.from_epsg(4326):
                    raise ValueError("This clip expects a source grid in EPSG:4326.")
                requested = from_bounds(*bbox, transform=source.transform)
                left, top = math.floor(requested.col_off), math.floor(requested.row_off)
                right = math.ceil(requested.col_off + requested.width)
                bottom = math.ceil(requested.row_off + requested.height)
                window = Window(left, top, right - left, bottom - top).intersection(
                    Window(0, 0, source.width, source.height)
                )
                values = source.read(1, window=window, masked=True)
                if not values.count():
                    raise EmptyClipError(f"The clip has no valid pixels: {item.id}")
                directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

def portolan(catalog_dir: Path, *arguments: str, credentials=None):
    """Run the CLI with only the settings supplied for this operation."""
    executable = Path(sys.executable).with_name("portolan")
    if not executable.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError("Run uv sync to install Portolan.")
    environment = {
        "PATH": f"{executable.parent}:/usr/bin:/bin",
        "AWS_CONFIG_FILE": "/dev/null",
        "AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE": "/dev/null",
        "AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED": "true",
    }
    if credentials:
        environment.update(
            {
                "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID": credentials["access"],
                "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY": credentials["secret"],
                "AWS_REGION": credentials["region"],
                "PORTOLAN_S3_ENDPOINT": require_https(credentials["endpoint"]),
                "PORTOLAN_S3_USE_SSL": "true",
            }
        )
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            [str(executable), *arguments],
            cwd=catalog_dir,
            env=environment,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=600,
        )
        if result.returncode:
            # CLI errors can contain storage URLs. Do not copy them into output.
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Portolan {arguments[0]} failed (exit {result.returncode})."
            )
        return result
    finally:
        environment.clear()

def publication_items(catalog_dir, products, bucket, prefix, data_url=None):
    """Set asset and document locations before the Portolan upload."""
    validate_prefix(prefix, "public" if data_url else "published")
    items = []
    files = {}
    for product in products:
        path = product["item_path"]
        document = json.loads(path.read_text())
        for asset in document["assets"].values():
            local = (path.parent / asset["href"]).resolve()
            relative = local.relative_to(catalog_dir.resolve()).as_posix()
            if not local.is_file():
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    "A STAC asset is missing from the local catalog."
                )
            key = f"{prefix}/{relative}"
            files[key] = local
            asset["href"] = f"s3://{bucket}/{key}"
            asset.pop("alternate", None)
            if data_url:
                asset["alternate"] = {"https": {"href": public_url(data_url, key)}}
            asset["file:size"] = local.stat().st_size
            # Multihash: sha2-256 code, digest length, digest.
            asset["file:checksum"] = "1220" + sha256(local)
        document["stac_extensions"] = list(
            dict.fromkeys(
                document.get("stac_extensions", [])
                + [
                    *([ALTERNATE_SCHEMA] if data_url else []),
                    "https://stac-extensions.github.io/file/v2.1.0/schema.json",
                ]
            )
        )
        # Keep the item table independent of its local directory.
        targets = {
            "self": path,
            "parent": catalog_dir / document["collection"] / "collection.json",
            "collection": catalog_dir / document["collection"] / "collection.json",
            "root": catalog_dir / "catalog.json",
        }
        document["links"] = [
            link for link in document["links"] if link["rel"] not in targets
        ]
        for rel, target in targets.items():
            key = f"{prefix}/{target.relative_to(catalog_dir).as_posix()}"
            document["links"].append(
                {
                    "rel": rel,
                    "href": public_url(data_url, key)
                    if data_url
                    else f"s3://{bucket}/{key}",
                    "type": "application/json",
                }
            )
        path.write_text(json.dumps(document, indent=2) + "\n")
        items.append(pystac.Item.from_dict(document))
    portolan(catalog_dir, "stac-geoparquet", "--collection", items[0].collection_id)
    return items, files

    def __init__(self, api_url, workspace, token_provider):
        self.api_url = require_https(api_url)
        self.workspace = workspace
        self._token_provider = token_provider
        self._session = requests.Session()
        self._session.trust_env = False
        self._credentials = None
        self._s3 = None

    def _json(self, method, url, **kwargs):
        try:
            response = self._session.request(
                method, url, timeout=30, allow_redirects=False, **kwargs
            )
            if response.status_code != 200:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"Workspace login or lookup failed (HTTP {response.status_code})."
                )
            return response.json()
        except requests.RequestException:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Cannot reach the workspace login or API service."
            ) from None

    def connect(self):
        if self._s3:
            self._s3.close()
            self._s3 = None
        if self._credentials:
            self._credentials.clear()
        token = self._token_provider()
        workspace = self._json(
            "GET",
            f"{self.api_url}/{quote(self.workspace, safe='')}",
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
        )
        credentials = workspace.get("storage", {}).get("credentials")
        if not credentials or credentials["bucketname"] != self.workspace:
            raise PermissionError(
                "The client must have storage access to the target workspace."
            )
        self._credentials = credentials
        self._s3 = boto3.client(
            "s3",
            endpoint_url=require_https(credentials["endpoint"]),
            aws_access_key_id=credentials["access"],
            aws_secret_access_key=credentials["secret"],
            region_name=credentials["region"],
            config=Config(
                signature_version="s3v4",
                s3={"addressing_style": "path"},
                connect_timeout=10,
                read_timeout=120,
            ),
        )

            f"s3://{self.workspace}/{prefix}",
            "--concurrency",
            "2",

            target_prefix,

        )

        pq.write_table(targets, directory / "public.destination.lock.parquet")

                Bucket=self.workspace,
                Key=key,
                Body=body,

def transfer_oci(package_dir, host, repository):
    """Run the registry push and digest-pinned pull in the workspace vCluster."""
    suffix = secrets.token_hex(4)
    configmap_name, job_name = f"catalog-package-{suffix}", f"catalog-publish-{suffix}"
    binary_data = {
        path.name: base64.b64encode(path.read_bytes()).decode("ascii")
        for path in package_dir.iterdir() if path.is_file()
    }
    # The three-Item demo fits one ConfigMap; stop before the API's size limit.
    if sum(len(value) for value in binary_data.values()) > 900_000:
        raise ValueError("The metadata package is too large for the demo input ConfigMap.")
    resource = {
        "apiVersion": "v1", "kind": "ConfigMap",
        "metadata": {"name": configmap_name, "labels": {"app": "cng-stac-publisher"}},
        "binaryData": binary_data,
    }
    values = {
        "PUBLISH_JOB": job_name, "PACKAGE_CONFIGMAP": configmap_name,
        "OCI_REFERENCE": f"{host}/{repository}:sha256-{sha256(package_dir / 'items.parquet')[:16]}",
    }
    rendered = json.dumps(resource) + "\n---\n" + render_manifest(
        (MANIFEST_DIR / "09-publisher-job.yaml").read_text(), values,
    )
    kube("apply", "-f", "-", input_text=rendered)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 660
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        status = json.loads(kube("get", "job", job_name, "-o", "json").stdout).get("status", {})
        if status.get("succeeded"):
            break
        if status.get("failed"):
            raise RuntimeError(f"Publisher Job {job_name} failed; inspect its logs in {NAMESPACE}.")
        time.sleep(5)
    else:
        raise TimeoutError(f"Publisher Job {job_name} did not finish.")
    logs = kube("logs", f"job/{job_name}").stdout
    result = json.loads(next(line.removeprefix("OCI_RESULT=") for line in logs.splitlines()
                             if line.startswith("OCI_RESULT=")))
    if result["hashes"] != package_hashes(package_dir):
        raise ValueError("The registry package differs from the local package.")
    kube("delete", "job", job_name)
    kube("delete", "configmap", configmap_name)
    return result["reference"]

def check_api(api_root, collection_id, expected_items, bbox):
    """Search the published Items and compare their metadata."""
    with requests.Session() as session:
        session.trust_env = False
        response = session.get(
            api_root + "/search",
            params={"collections": collection_id, "bbox": ",".join(map(str, bbox)), "limit": 100},
            timeout=60,
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        features = response.json()["features"]
    if {feature["id"] for feature in features} != {item.id for item in expected_items}:
        raise ValueError("The API search did not return the uploaded Items.")
    check_items(features, expected_items)
    return features


def check_items(features, expected_items):
    expected = {item.id: item.to_dict(transform_hrefs=False) for item in expected_items}
    for feature in features:
        original = expected[feature["id"]]
        # Catalogs can write the same polygon with a different vertex order.
        assert shape(feature["geometry"]).equals(shape(original["geometry"]))
        assert feature["bbox"] == original["bbox"]
        for key in ("datetime", "start_datetime", "end_datetime"):
            assert datetime.fromisoformat(
                feature["properties"][key]
            ) == datetime.fromisoformat(original["properties"][key])
        for key in ("proj:shape", "proj:transform"):
            assert feature["properties"][key] == original["properties"][key]
        assert set(feature["assets"]) == set(original["assets"])
        for key, asset in feature["assets"].items():
            expected_asset = original["assets"][key]
            # Shared GeoParquet schemas can add null alternate fields.
            actual_alternates = {k: v for k, v in asset.get("alternate", {}).items() if v is not None}
            expected_alternates = {k: v for k, v in expected_asset.get("alternate", {}).items() if v is not None}
            assert actual_alternates == expected_alternates
            assert asset["file:checksum"] == expected_asset["file:checksum"]
            if asset["href"].startswith("s3://"):
                assert asset["href"] == expected_asset["href"]
            else:
                actual = urlsplit(asset["href"])
                public = urlsplit(
                    (expected_asset.get("alternate", {}).get("https") or {})
                    .get("href", expected_asset["href"])
                )
                assert (actual.scheme, actual.netloc, actual.path) == (
                    public.scheme,
                    public.netloc,
                    public.path,
                )

    with requests.Session() as session:
        session.trust_env = False
        for feature in features:
            for asset in feature["assets"].values():
                url = asset["href"]
                if not url.startswith("https://"):
                    url = asset["alternate"]["https"]["href"]
                headers = {"Origin": origin} if origin else {}
                response = session.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=120)

                        f"Public asset download failed (HTTP {response.status_code})."

def relocation_locks(items, bucket, source_prefix, target_prefix, endpoint):
    """Keep asset paths when planning the copy from published/ to public/."""
    from stacpkg.assets import asset_lock_table, derive_asset_lock

    validate_prefix(source_prefix, "published")
    validate_prefix(target_prefix, "public")
    table = stac_geoparquet.arrow.parse_stac_items_to_arrow(
        [item.to_dict(transform_hrefs=False) for item in items]
    ).read_all()
    sources, targets = [], []
    for row in derive_asset_lock(
        table, probe_metadata=False, include_metadata_assets=True
    ).to_pylist():
        if (
            row["store_type"] != "s3"
            or row["store_container"] != bucket
            or not row["key"].startswith(source_prefix + "/")
        ):
            raise ValueError("Relocate only assets from this published dataset.")
        relative = row["key"][len(source_prefix) + 1 :]
        if any(part in {"", ".", ".."} for part in relative.split("/")):

        targets.append({**source, "key": f"{target_prefix}/{relative}"})

def stage_index(destination="/data/items.parquet"):
    """Fetch and check the uploaded item table before the first API starts."""
    import hashlib
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    from urllib.parse import urlsplit
    import requests

    target = Path(destination)
    href = os.environ["INDEX_HREF"]
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    try:
        if href.startswith("s3://"):
            import boto3
            from botocore.config import Config

            location = urlsplit(href)
            client = boto3.client(
                "s3",
                endpoint_url=os.environ["AWS_ENDPOINT_URL"],
                aws_access_key_id=os.environ["AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"],
                aws_secret_access_key=os.environ["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"],
                region_name=os.environ["AWS_REGION"],
                config=Config(s3={"addressing_style": "path"}),
            )
            try:
                response = client.get_object(
                    Bucket=location.netloc, Key=location.path.lstrip("/")
                )
                with response["Body"] as body, target.open("wb") as output:
                    for chunk in iter(lambda: body.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
                        digest.update(chunk)
                        output.write(chunk)
            finally:
                client.close()
        elif href.startswith("https://"):
            with requests.Session() as session:
                session.trust_env = False
                with session.get(href, stream=True, timeout=120) as response:
                    response.raise_for_status()
                    with target.open("wb") as output:
                        for chunk in response.iter_content(1024 * 1024):
                            digest.update(chunk)
                            output.write(chunk)
        else:
            raise ValueError("Use an S3 or HTTPS item-table location.")
        if digest.hexdigest() != os.environ["INDEX_SHA256"]:
            raise ValueError("The item-table checksum differs.")
    except Exception:
        target.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise RuntimeError("Cannot fetch and verify the STAC item table.") from None

def forward_api(service, port, previous=None):
    """Start a local Kubernetes proxy for one Service."""
    if previous is not None and previous.poll() is None:
        previous.terminate()
        previous.wait(timeout=10)
    process = subprocess.Popen(
        [*KUBECTL, "proxy", f"--port={port}", "--address=127.0.0.1", "--append-server-path"],
        env=human_kube_env(), stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    )
    root = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}{proxy_path(service)}"
    try:
        with requests.Session() as session:
            session.trust_env = False
            for attempt in range(60):
                if process.poll() is not None:
                    raise RuntimeError(f"Kubernetes proxy stopped; check port {port} and vc0 access.")
                try:
                    response = session.get(root + "/", timeout=3)
                    if response.ok and response.headers.get("content-type", "").startswith("application/json"):
                        display(HTML(f'<a href="{escape(root + "/", quote=True)}" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open {service}</a>'))
                        return process, root
                except requests.RequestException:
                    pass
                time.sleep(1)
        raise TimeoutError(f"The {service} API did not become ready.")
    except BaseException:
        if process.poll() is None:
            process.terminate()
            process.wait(timeout=10)
        raise

            raise RuntimeError(
                "The public catalogue or asset route needs CORS for " + origin

docs.title: Register STAC metadata¶
docs.text:
Alice publishes three Sentinel-5P cloud fraction clips in ws-alice. She uses Portolan to create metadata and upload files, then stacpkg to copy the assets from published/ to public/.

Run these steps in order:

  1. Publish the clips and start a STAC search API.
  2. Copy the assets to public/, update their links, and check public downloads.
  3. Push the public metadata to a registry in the workspace vCluster and start a second API from its digest.

Cloud fraction values run from 0 (clear) to 1 (fully cloudy). The source is the DLR GeoService catalogue. Each run selects three recent usable observations.

docs.title: Data flow¶
docs.text: The two search APIs run in Alice's workspace vCluster, using the kubeconfig from Workspace API. PackageR serves the public catalogue and downloads through the workspace Data service.

docs.title: 1. Connect to the workspace vCluster¶
docs.text:
Run this notebook from a repository checkout:

uv sync
uv run jupyter lab docs/getting-started/register-stac-metadata.ipynb

Sign in as Alice. Workspace API supplies storage credentials and the ws-alice/vc0/demo kubeconfig. The profile selects stac-fastapi-pgstac, as configured in the example resources. The notebook keeps the caller token in a private temporary file and checks namespace access before deployment.

Step 10 deploys CNCF Distribution with a persistent volume in the same namespace. A Job pushes the metadata package to its internal Service. Workspace workloads can read and write this demo registry; it has no public route or separate login. The helper functions are in collapsible cells. The workflow cells show the publication and deployment calls.

docs.title: 2. Find recent observations¶
docs.text: Read up to 30 recent Items from the DLR GeoService STAC API. Select three different days with valid pixels around Vienna. A bounding-box search finds intersecting Items; the next step clips their files.

docs.title: 3. Clip the data¶
docs.text:
Read the cf assets with HTTP range requests. Keep whole source pixels that cover the requested box. This preserves the grid, NoData, and values. Output bounds can extend by one pixel beyond the requested box.

Write a COG, preview, and thumbnail for each day. Previews map zero to black and one to white; they do not change the COG values.

docs.title: 4. Describe the clips with Portolan¶
docs.text: Create STAC metadata and a GeoParquet table for the clips. Check the times, cropped grid, attribution, and file hashes. Initial asset links use private s3://<workspace>/published/... locations.

docs.title: 5. Upload under published/¶
docs.text: The upload uses Alice's token with GET /workspaces/ws-alice to obtain backing S3 credentials. The management notebook shows this call directly. Upload the catalogue and assets with Portolan, then compare their hashes with the local files. Keep storage settings out of notebook output.

docs.title: 6. Start the first search API¶
docs.text:
Apply the first API manifests in the workspace vCluster. The API downloads the private item table with a storage Secret and checks its hash.

Start a local Kubernetes Service proxy and search the uploaded Items. Asset links still point to private S3 files. Use the link below to open the API.

docs.title: 7. Copy the assets to public/¶
docs.text:
Use stacpkg relocation to copy the assets within the workspace bucket. Keep the published/ files and check that both copies match. Matching destination files can be reused; different content stops the run.

Set the primary asset links to permanent PackageR HTTP routes. Keep public S3 locations as alternate links. Update the shared public/catalog.parquet table.

docs.title: 8. Search the public metadata¶
docs.text: Restart the first API with the public item-table URL. Remove its storage Secret after the Pod is ready. Check search results, public downloads, and byte-range reads. The link below uses the local Kubernetes proxy.

docs.title: 9. Open the public catalogue¶
docs.text: PackageR serves Collection and Item links from public/catalog.parquet. It has no /search route. Check its Items, public asset downloads, and browser access from MoreGeo, then open the links below.

docs.title: 10. Push the metadata package¶
docs.text:
Deploy CNCF Distribution with the registry resources. Its 1 GiB volume keeps artifacts across Pod restarts. The internal Service uses HTTP and has no separate login or public route. Use it for trusted workspace workloads.

Package the public item table, asset lock, and Collection metadata. A publisher Job receives these small metadata files through a temporary ConfigMap, pushes them, and pulls them by digest. Compare its returned hashes with the local files. Image bytes stay in workspace storage.

docs.title: 11. Start an API from the package digest¶
docs.text: Apply the OCI API manifests. An init container pulls the package from Distribution into a shared volume and reports its file hashes. Compare those hashes and repeat the search and download checks. Open the second API with the local proxy link below.

docs.title: 12. Keep or remove the API resources¶
docs.text:
The APIs and registry stay available by default. The local proxies use your caller token. Rerun the relevant API cell to renew access after it expires. Set CLEAN_UP = True to stop the proxies and remove this notebook's workloads, Services, ConfigMaps, and Secrets.

The registry PVC and its OCI artifacts stay available. Delete the PVC separately when you no longer need them. The published/ source files, public/ copies, and shared catalogue also stay in workspace storage.

docs.title: Search and export a catalog with managed PostgreSQL¶
docs.text:
Alice deploys STAC FastAPI PgSTAC in ws-alice/vc0, registers three NAIP Items, and searches them with pystac-client. She then exchanges her login for a token limited to the demo profile. That token submits a GeoParquet export Job through a downloaded kubeconfig.

The API uses the managed catalog PostgreSQL database. The export writes exports/naip.parquet to Alice's workspace bucket.
