docs.title: 1. Sign in and download Alice's profile¶
docs.text:
Use ws-alice with vc0, the managed catalog database, and its managed-postgres Secret binding in stac-fastapi-pgstac. See Alice's Datalab.

uv sync
uv run jupyter lab docs/getting-started/stac-fastapi-pgstac.ipynb

Sign in as Alice through device login. The Workspace API supplies the ready vc0/demo kubeconfig. It contains connection settings; the caller supplies an access token separately. No operator-supplied or host-cluster kubeconfig is needed.

Alice's human token includes her virtual cluster administrator role. Selecting the demo profile does not reduce that role. Step 9 checks the permissions of the exchanged token.

docs.title: 2. Install PgSTAC and start the API¶
docs.text:
Keep the generated API password in a separate Kubernetes Secret. Reuse that Secret on another run. Neither the notebook nor its output contains the managed PostgreSQL password.

The migration Job uses the admin login once. The API receives only the database host, port, database name, and its own stac_catalog login. The pgstac_ingest role permits the registration calls in step 4.

docs.title: 3. Open the API through Kubernetes¶
docs.text:
Start kubectl proxy on 127.0.0.1. Requests use Alice's vc0 profile and the Kubernetes Service proxy. This route does not need port-forward streaming.

Keep this process running while you use the notebook. The links below open the API through the same local proxy.

docs.title: 4. Register the example catalog¶
docs.text:
Convert the three GeoParquet rows to STAC Items. Keep their source asset links. This step copies metadata into PostgreSQL; it does not download or upload the image files. Some source assets need a signed URL from their original service.

Read the source Collection for its license and providers, then set its extent to these three sample Items. Use POST for a new record and PUT for an existing record, so another run keeps the same Item IDs.

docs.title: 5. List Collections and Items with pystac-client¶
docs.text: pystac-client is the Python HTTP client for this STAC API. PgSTAC runs its searches in PostgreSQL. The client reads all pages when a response contains only part of the result.

docs.title: 6. Search by area, date, and Item ID¶
docs.text: The small bounding box intersects only the eastern sample Item. The date filter selects the two Items from 20 August. A search outside the source area returns no Items.

docs.title: 7. Inspect an Item¶
docs.text: Fetch an Item by its Collection and ID. Compare its geometry and asset metadata with the sample to check that registration kept their values. The API omits null optional fields in band descriptions. Ignore those null object fields in the comparison. The API supplies new navigation links for this local catalog.

docs.title: 8. Read PostgreSQL directly¶
docs.text: The psql client manifest uses the same managed Secret. The code below runs a short query in vc0 and reads its Pod log. The password stays in Kubernetes.

docs.title: 9. Exchange Alice's token for the demo profile¶
docs.text:
Request ws-alice:vclusters_vc0_demo from the Workspace token endpoint. The response keeps Alice's user subject and grants only ws_api and vcluster_vc0_demo.

Download the demo profile through Workspace API with that token, then use both for Kubernetes access. Check that it can create Jobs in stac-fastapi-pgstac and cannot create cluster roles or list Pods in kube-system. Token values and temporary file paths stay out of output.

docs.title: 10. Submit a GeoParquet export Job¶
docs.text:
Use the scoped token to install the export script and CronJob, then start one Job from that template. The Job exports the three NAIP Items and writes exports/naip.parquet to workspace storage. Check the exported IDs, geometry, and file checksum.

The CronJob is set to hourly UTC and starts suspended. Set ENABLE_SCHEDULE = True to enable it. Its Pods use a storage Secret, with no human or exchanged token. This example copies current storage credentials; refresh that Secret after credential rotation, or use the provider's s3:primary Secret binding for managed updates.

The exchanged token is for submitting and inspecting the Job. Its expiry does not stop an accepted Job or the Kubernetes schedule. A later external submission needs a fresh token exchange.

docs.title: 11. Stop the local proxy¶
docs.text: Set STOP_FORWARD = True when you finish. The API and database stay available.

docs.title: Access a workspace virtual cluster
docs.text:
Use the workspace dashboard to download a kubeconfig. Use your own identity for interactive work, or give a process an exchanged token for one access profile. Downloading a kubeconfig does not grant or reduce permissions.

The Provider Datalab guide explains the generated profiles, direct operator downloads, login cache, and revocation. This guide shows the Workspace API and UI flow.

The examples use Alice’s workspace in eoepca-demo:

Setting Value Dashboard Alice’s workspace Virtual cluster vc0 Administrator profile cluster-admin, all namespaces Delegation profile demo, Kubernetes edit in stac-fastapi-pgstac Delegation scope ws-alice:vclusters_vc0_demo

Install kubectl and Python 3. Use Bash for the shell commands. For the token exchange script, run uv sync from this repository first.

docs.title: How Workspace API supplies access
docs.text:
The provider publishes ready profiles and OAuth2 client references. Workspace API checks your workspace permissions, reads the referenced connection Secrets, and supplies the permitted values to the dashboard. You do not need a host-cluster kubeconfig or Kubernetes Secret access.

The Virtual clusters card provides Download kubeconfig. The separate OAuth2 card provides the workspace client credentials. Users with ws_access or ws_admin can retrieve these values. A caller with only ws_api can retrieve service connections, including ready vcluster profiles, but cannot retrieve OAuth2 client credentials.

A download selects an API endpoint and default namespace. The access token and Kubernetes RBAC determine what the caller can do. Provider Datalab automatically grants workspace administrators ws_admin and the built-in vcluster_<instance>_cluster-admin role for each configured instance. Alice therefore already has vcluster_vc0_cluster-admin; no separate role assignment is needed. The virtual API checks this vcluster role, while ws_admin controls workspace management.

docs.title: 1. Download the administrator profile
docs.text:
Sign in to the dashboard as Alice. In Virtual clusters, expand the ready vc0 entry with the cluster-admin profile. Select Download kubeconfig. Rename the downloaded file to ws-alice-vc0.kubeconfig in your working directory. The generated download name can include a hash.

Download a current kubeconfig to use offline login. Older downloads keep their embedded helper and login scopes until you replace them.

The profile supports device login. Alice’s issued token must contain vcluster_vc0_cluster-admin for administrator access.

docs.title: 2. Supply the OAuth2 client secret locally
docs.text:
In OAuth2, expand the ready ws-alice client and copy its client secret. Use the clientSecret field. Save only the secret value, without a JSON or YAML wrapper. This command asks for it without displaying it or putting it in shell history:

umask 077
unset DATALAB_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE
python3 - <<'PY'
from getpass import getpass
from pathlib import Path

directory = Path.home() / ".config/datalab"
directory.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
path = directory / "ws-alice-client-secret"
value = getpass("Workspace OAuth2 client secret: ")
if not value:
    raise SystemExit("The client secret is required.")
path.touch(mode=0o600, exist_ok=True)
path.chmod(0o600)
path.write_text(value)
PY
export DATALAB_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE="$HOME/.config/datalab/ws-alice-client-secret"

The secret authenticates the OAuth client. The browser login identifies Alice and selects her user permissions. The kubeconfig contains neither a client secret nor a user token.

docs.title: 3. Start kubectl and approve the device login
docs.text:
kubectl --kubeconfig ./ws-alice-vc0.kubeconfig get namespaces
kubectl --kubeconfig ./ws-alice-vc0.kubeconfig \
  auth can-i '*' '*' --all-namespaces

On the first call, the embedded helper prints a verification URL and a user code. Open the URL, enter the code, sign in as Alice, and approve the request. The waiting command then continues. The authorization check must return yes for Alice’s administrator role.

The browser login to the dashboard and this kubectl login are separate OAuth flows. An existing browser session can simplify approval, but it does not populate the kubectl token cache.

docs.title: 4. Reuse the cached login
docs.text:
The current helper requests openid offline_access ws-alice:interactive. It saves the access token, offline refresh token, and local login deadline in ~/.cache/datalab/oidc/<hash>.json. It uses $XDG_CACHE_HOME/datalab/oidc when set, or DATALAB_TOKEN_CACHE_DIR for an explicit directory. The directory has mode 0700; cache files have mode 0600. The client secret is not stored there.

Credential or session Lifetime Access token 5 minutes in the tested demo login. CLI cached login Up to 30 days after device approval. Refresh does not extend this local deadline. Offline session Subject to Keycloak’s offline idle and maximum limits and revocation. Provider Datalab sets a 30-day client idle limit. Its 30-day client maximum applies when the realm enables Offline Session Max Limited. Shorter realm limits can end access sooner.

When kubectl runs near access-token expiry, the helper attempts renewal with the cached offline refresh token and client secret. Successful renewal needs no browser approval. Keep DATALAB_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE set for refresh; set it again in a new shell. There is no background refresh while kubectl is idle. After the local deadline or an invalid_grant response, the helper starts device login again. Other renewal errors stop the command. The provider guide describes how to start a fresh device login.

Ordinary browser logout does not revoke offline access. Revoke the workspace client’s offline access in Keycloak to stop further refresh. An already issued access token can remain usable until its expiry. See the provider’s human login lifetime and Keycloak offline access for the session settings and revocation controls.

The notebooks use a separate public-client login and keep tokens in kernel memory. Passing one of those tokens through DATALAB_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE does not use this offline cache. See notebook logins.

If your user has only an additional namespace role, the administrator profile can still perform device login. Request the matching optional scope as shown under human access. The resulting token grants that namespace role. It does not grant cluster administration.

docs.title: Case 2: Delegate the demo profile to a process
docs.text: Alice remains the human identity in the exchanged token. The process gets the demo kubeconfig and the exchanged access token. Alice keeps her original login and any client credentials.

docs.title: 1. Download the demo profile
docs.text:
In Alice’s dashboard, expand Virtual clusters > vc0 > demo and select Download kubeconfig. Save it as ws-alice-vcluster-vc0_demo.kubeconfig. Check that the displayed namespace is stac-fastapi-pgstac and the role is edit.

The profile uses --token-only. It cannot start device login or refresh a token. Giving it Alice’s unrestricted token would retain her wider access.

docs.title: 2. Exchange Alice’s user token
docs.text:
Run this script from the repository root. It uses the same public client and device login as the notebooks. Approve the login as Alice. This approval is for the delegator; the recipient will have no login prompt.

umask 077
uv run python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "docs")
from notebook_support import ApiSession, load_config, workspace_login

config = load_config("eoepca-demo.env", "workspace")
tokens = workspace_login(config, "alice")
with ApiSession() as api:
    response = api.get(
        config["WORKSPACE_API_ENDPOINT"] + "/ws-alice/token",
        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + tokens["access_token"]},
        params={"scope": "ws-alice:vclusters_vc0_demo"},
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    delegated = response.json()

path = Path("ws-alice-vc0-demo.token")
path.touch(mode=0o600, exist_ok=True)
path.chmod(0o600)
path.write_text(delegated["access_token"])
print(f"Saved {path}; expires in {delegated['expires_in']} seconds.")
PY

Workspace API performs token exchange with its stored workspace client credentials. It checks the returned signature, issuer, subject, audiences, scopes, and roles before returning the token. Alice needs token-issuance permission, ws_api, and vcluster_vc0_demo. The resulting workspace roles are ws_api and vcluster_vc0_demo; administrator roles are absent.

The scope query is required. A call to /ws-alice/token without it requests a service-account token with only ws_api, which cannot access the virtual cluster. See the Workspace token API.

docs.title: 3. Give the files to the process and run kubectl
docs.text:
Transfer the kubeconfig and token file through a private channel. On the recipient’s machine, in the directory with both files:

unset DATALAB_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE
export DATALAB_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE="$PWD/ws-alice-vc0-demo.token"
chmod 600 "$DATALAB_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE"
kubectl --kubeconfig ./ws-alice-vcluster-vc0_demo.kubeconfig \
  -n stac-fastapi-pgstac get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Running
kubectl --kubeconfig ./ws-alice-vcluster-vc0_demo.kubeconfig \
  -n stac-fastapi-pgstac auth can-i create deployments

The first call lists running Pods without a login prompt. The authorization check returns yes. DATALAB_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE is the path to a file that contains only the JWT, without Bearer or a JSON wrapper. It is not the token value.

docs.title: 4. Check that other namespaces are denied
docs.text:
kubectl --kubeconfig ./ws-alice-vcluster-vc0_demo.kubeconfig \
  -n kube-system get pods
kubectl --kubeconfig ./ws-alice-vcluster-vc0_demo.kubeconfig \
  auth can-i create namespaces

The Pod request must fail with Forbidden. The second check returns no and a nonzero exit status. The token permits edit operations only in stac-fastapi-pgstac, unless that identity has another applicable Kubernetes binding. Its ws_api role also permits service credential reads through Workspace API; the namespace restriction applies to Kubernetes access.

These checks passed on eoepca-demo on 2026-11-07. This image shows the recorded command output from that run:

docs.title: 5. Replace the token when it expires
docs.text:
The token’s exp claim sets its expiry. The script reports the issuer’s expires_in; it does not promise a fixed duration. The recipient has no refresh token, uses no device-login cache, and must obtain a new exchange result from Alice or the issuing service after expiry.

The virtual API validates JWTs locally. Keycloak logout, removal of Alice’s role, revocation of offline access, client-secret rotation, or deletion of a token file does not reliably invalidate copies of an issued token before exp. There is no individual JWT revocation list in this setup. An operator can remove the profile or its RBAC binding to deny access sooner, after reconciliation. This affects every caller that needs that profile or binding. See lifetime and revocation.

def sha256(path: Path) -> str:

    with path.open("rb") as stream:

def prepare_image(source_item, destination):
    if FIXTURE_DIR is not None:
        source = Path(FIXTURE_DIR) / source_item.id / "overview.tif"
        if not source.is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(source)
        # The fixture already contains a Vienna clip. Leave the source file intact.
        copy_raster(source, destination, driver="COG", compress="DEFLATE")
        return

    temporary = destination.parent / "clipped.tif"
    try:
        with rasterio.Env(
            GDAL_DISABLE_READDIR_ON_OPEN="EMPTY_DIR",
            CPL_VSIL_CURL_ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS=".tif,.tiff",
        ), rasterio.open(source_item.assets["visual"].href) as source:
            bounds = transform_bounds("EPSG:4326", source.crs, *VIENNA_BBOX, densify_pts=21)
            window = from_bounds(*bounds, transform=source.transform)
            window = window.round_offsets().round_lengths().intersection(
                Window(0, 0, source.width, source.height)
            )
            pixels = source.read(window=window)
            profile = source.profile.copy()
            profile.update(
                driver="GTiff", width=pixels.shape[2], height=pixels.shape[1],
                transform=window_transform(window, source.transform),
                tiled=True, blockxsize=512, blockysize=512, compress="DEFLATE",
            )
            with rasterio.open(temporary, "w", **profile) as target:
                target.write(pixels)
                target.colorinterp = source.colorinterp
            copy_raster(temporary, destination, driver="COG", compress="DEFLATE",
                        overview_resampling="AVERAGE")
    finally:
        temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)

docs.title: Vienna imagery with STAC and S3¶
docs.text:
Alice publishes three Sentinel-2 image crops in ws-alice. She creates STAC metadata, uploads the files, and checks public and S3 downloads.

Use an existing workspace with storage and a Data service. Change the workspace name and owner below for your own workspace. Files under public/ are publicly readable.

PackageR reads public/catalog.parquet and serves Collection and Item links. It has no /search route.

docs.title: Data flow¶
docs.text: Crop the three scenes and upload the images, previews, and catalogue through the backing S3 service. PackageR supplies public catalogue links and image downloads. Python S3 clients and the AWS CLI read the same files through the Data endpoint with the owner's token. The notebook compares downloaded files with their local SHA-256 checksums.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the runtime¶
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv sync
uv run jupyter lab docs/getting-started/vienna-imagery-with-stac-and-s3.ipynb

Use eoepca-demo.env for public service addresses. Sign in as Alice when prompted. No Kubernetes access is needed. Tokens and storage credentials stay in kernel memory.

Install the AWS CLI for step 6.

docs.title: 2. Select the scenes¶
docs.text:
Use three fixed scene IDs from February, May, and August. The reported cloud cover applies to each source tile. It can differ from the cloud cover over Vienna.

Crop each image to the Vienna bounding box and write a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF with a PNG preview. Keep the cropped grid in the STAC metadata. The August scene uses a different tile, so its available crop differs.

docs.title: 3. Write the STAC catalogue¶
docs.text:
The public share reads public/catalog.parquet. Asset paths must be relative to public, such as vienna-s2l2a-26/<scene-id>/overview.tif. PackageR turns those paths into public download links in returned STAC Items.

The catalogue records the source scene links, license, and cropped grid. It contains colour imagery and previews; use the original reflectance bands for numerical analysis.

docs.title: 4. Upload via backing S3¶
docs.text:
Sign in as the workspace owner with device login. The Workspace API supplies its backing storage credentials. The Data S3 endpoint used later is read only.

Skip image files with matching hashes and stop if an image key has different content. Merge these three Items into the shared catalogue and retain its other datasets. Update the catalogue after the assets; a conditional write stops if another writer changed it.

docs.title: 5. Browse STAC and download via the PackageR HTTP API¶
docs.text:
The public share reads public/catalog.parquet. Follow its Item links to the images. This catalogue has no /search endpoint.

The shared catalogue can contain other datasets. Select these three scene IDs, download a COG and preview, and compare their checksums with the local files. Optional asset columns for other datasets can contain null values.

docs.title: Browse the PackageR catalogue¶
docs.text:
PackageR builds a catalogue from the uploaded STAC GeoParquet file at /api/public/catalog/public. It serves a Collection and its Items through the existing Data service. This catalogue has no /search route. See the notebook guide for the two STAC search APIs.

Open it in STAC Browser to view the three scenes on a map and browse their image assets.

docs.title: 6. Read and download via S3¶
docs.text:
Refresh Alice's login. Use the workspace name for both S3 signing fields and the access token for the session-token field. The Data S3 endpoint supports reads.

Check a byte-range read, all seven files, and an AWS CLI download. If the login has expired, repeat step 4.

docs.title: Result¶
docs.text: The workspace holds three COG images, three PNG previews, and one catalogue. The public image and preview downloads, all seven S3 downloads, and the CLI image download match the local SHA-256 checksums. A byte-range request returns the requested part of an image.

docs.title: Notebook guide
docs.text:
Workspace Management creates a workspace and shows its API operations. Vienna publishes images. The STAC notebooks add search and package metadata. The saved runs were checked with Provider Datalab 0.12.0-rc.8 on eoepca-demo.

Notebook Use it to What it checks Workspace Management Create a workspace, access its virtual cluster, add and delegate a namespace profile, push an OCI package, and share a file. Namespace access and denial, registry push and pull, and temporary and public file downloads. STAC with managed PostgreSQL Deploy as Alice, search the sample catalog, and submit a GeoParquet export with an exchanged token. Searches and metadata match. The token permits Jobs in the selected namespace and denies cluster administration. The exported IDs, geometry, and checksum match. Vienna imagery with STAC and S3 Crop satellite images, publish STAC metadata, and use public downloads and authenticated S3 clients. The STAC items describe the cropped images. Public, S3, and AWS CLI downloads have matching checksums. Byte-range reads return the requested bytes. Register STAC metadata Publish three Sentinel-5P cloud fraction clips, relocate them for public access, and serve STAC search. Source and public copies match. The clipped grids, API searches, HTTP downloads, and OCI package hashes are checked.

docs.title: Choose where to run
docs.text:
Use the existing ws-alice workspace, or a workspace with the same services. Run Workspace Management only if you need to create one.

Workspace Management creates its demo profile for namespace demo in the new workspace. The STAC notebooks use ws-alice/vc0/demo, which selects stac-fastapi-pgstac. The profiles belong to different workspaces.

Run Vienna from a repository checkout as Alice in ws-alice. It needs storage, a Data service, and the AWS CLI. No Kubernetes access is needed.

Run STAC with managed PostgreSQL as Alice in ws-alice/vc0. An operator first sets up the catalog database and managed-postgres Secret binding from setup/examples.yaml. Alice signs in and downloads the demo profile through Workspace API. She deploys the API with her human token, then exchanges it for namespace access and submits an export Job. The local Kubernetes Service proxy supports registration and search.

Run registration from a repository checkout as Alice. It downloads the same ws-alice/vc0/demo profile through Workspace API. Her login supplies Kubernetes and storage access. The notebook deploys CNCF Distribution with a 1 GiB volume and submits a publisher Job in that namespace. The registry has an internal HTTP Service for trusted workspace workloads, with no public route or separate login.

The notebooks use public settings from eoepca-demo.env. Tokens and storage credentials stay in kernel memory, except for private temporary token files used by the kubeconfig helper. Credential values stay out of saved output.

Workspace Management uses the default managed registry backed by workspace storage. Registration creates a separate Distribution registry inside vc0 to show package publication from Kubernetes Jobs. It keeps packages on its own persistent volume.

docs.title: Login and token lifetimes
docs.text:
The notebooks sign in through the public workspace-api client and keep the login in kernel memory. They pass short-lived access tokens to kubectl through private files. Rerun the login cell if the session expires; restarting the kernel starts a new login. These calls do not use the kubeconfig’s offline login cache.

For standalone kubectl work, the administrator kubeconfig can start device login and cache it for up to 30 days. See virtual cluster access. An exchanged namespace token has only its reported access-token lifetime and no refresh token. Offline login does not extend a delegated token.

docs.title: Publish images for other people to use
docs.text: Vienna publishes three Sentinel-2 crops, previews, and a STAC catalogue. PackageR serves Collection and Item links. Readers can download public assets without a workspace account. Workspace members can also read them with S3 tools.

docs.title: Process data and add search
docs.text:
Use STAC registration to prepare recent data for applications that need to search by area and date. It selects three recent usable Sentinel-5P cloud fraction observations from the DLR GeoService STAC endpoint and clips them around Vienna. Flow 1 uses Portolan to create the metadata and upload the files under published/. A first vCluster API searches those Items through a local Kubernetes Service proxy.

Flow 2 uses stacpkg relocation to copy the assets from published/ to public/ in the same workspace bucket and keeps the source files. The public metadata uses PackageR HTTP download routes as primary asset links, with public S3 locations as alternates. The first API restarts with this metadata. PackageR serves the public catalogue dynamically through the existing Data service. MoreGeo STAC Browser previews this catalogue in the user’s browser.

How readers get the metadata When to use it PackageR reads public/catalog.parquet and builds Collection and Item responses on request. Publish a catalogue through the existing Data service. Readers follow links; this view has no /search route. The first vCluster API fetches and verifies the uploaded GeoParquet at startup. Demonstrate search first with private published/ S3 asset links, then with relocated public HTTP links. A separate STAC API reads an OCI package pulled by an init container. Start an API with a known copy of the metadata. The package digest fixes that copy until you deploy a new digest.

Flow 3 bundles the public metadata and asset links into an OCI artifact. A Job pushes it to Distribution in the workspace vCluster and checks a pull by digest. The second API loads that same digest. Image bytes stay in workspace storage. The local proxies last while the notebook is running and its caller token is valid. The Data service and its PackageR catalogue remain available separately. Notebook cleanup keeps the registry PVC and its artifacts.

Each run selects three recent usable observations. It adds them to the shared catalogue and keeps older published data. It does not set up a schedule or delete old observations.

docs.title: Run the upload as a job
docs.text:
The registration notebook uses Alice’s interactive login. For a scheduled storage upload, use OAuth machine access and supply secrets through the job’s secret store. Its registry publisher Job uses the internal workspace Service.

The PgSTAC notebook includes an hourly GeoParquet export CronJob. It starts suspended and runs one Job for validation. Enable its schedule when needed. The Job uses a storage Secret; the exchanged token only submits and inspects it. Refresh the storage Secret after credential rotation or configure a provider Secret binding.
